meta.title_plain: How a quiet kid with a huge serve won 7 Wimbledons
meta.teaser: Pete Sampras hit balls against a wall, then built a serve nobody could break.

page.title: How a quiet kid with a huge serve won 7 Wimbledons
page.bigIdea: Pete Sampras changed his whole game as a teenager, even when it was hard. That brave switch helped him win 14 Grand Slams.

cards.title: A racket in the basement
cards.front: Pete was born in 1971 in Washington, D.C.
cards.back: At age 3, he found a tennis racket in his basement. He spent hours hitting balls against the wall. His hero was champion Rod Laver.
cards.tryit: Hit 50 balls against a wall today. Count how many in a row you keep going.

cards.title: The big switch at 14
cards.front: As a kid, Pete hit a two-handed backhand.
cards.back: At 14, he and coach Peter Fischer changed to a one-handed backhand and serve-and-volley. He struggled at first, but it paid off.
cards.tryit: Pick one shot you want to improve. Practice it 20 times, even if it feels weird.

cards.title: Meet "Pistol Pete"
cards.front: His serve was one of the best ever.
cards.back: It was clocked at over 200 km/h (120 mph). It was so strong that fans called him "Pistol Pete." Think of a one-shot sniper in Fortnite.
cards.tryit: Serve 10 balls. Aim each one at the same corner of the box.

cards.title: Youngest US Open champ
cards.front: In 1990, Pete won his first Grand Slam.
cards.back: He won the US Open at 19. He became its youngest-ever men's champion. Later he won seven Wimbledon titles in eight years.
cards.tryit: Write down one thing you can do now that you couldn't do a year ago.

cards.title: Calm wins big
cards.front: Pete was known for being quiet on court.
cards.back: He stayed calm under pressure. He was No. 1 at year's end six years in a row, 1993 to 1998. That's a record.
cards.tryit: Before your next serve, take one slow breath and picture where it will go.

words.d: Serving, then rushing to the net to hit the ball before it bounces.

quiz.q: How did little Pete first practise tennis?
quiz.hint: Think about the racket he found at home.
quiz.why: At age 3, he hit balls for hours against a wall in his basement.

quiz.q: What did Pete change at age 14?
opts: His backhand and style of play
quiz.hint: Look at idea 2. It was a hard change.
quiz.why: He switched to a one-handed backhand and a serve-and-volley game.

quiz.hint: Which shot was he most famous for?
quiz.why: His serve was so powerful and precise that it earned him the nickname.

quiz.q: Which tournament did Pete win seven times?
quiz.hint: It's played on grass in London.
quiz.why: He won Wimbledon seven times in eight years, from 1993 to 2000.

page.think: Pete changed his backhand at 14, even though it made him worse at first. Is there a part of your game you'd change if you knew it would pay off later?
